title: The economics of birthday parties
text: Parents in many cities now spend astonishing sums {{1}} children's birthday parties. Entertainers, themed cakes and hired venues can easily push the total {{2}} several hundred pounds. Sociologists trace the trend {{3}} social media, {{4}} images of elaborate parties circulate constantly, raising expectations. There is also an element of competition: no parent wishes to appear mean. Yet children themselves consistently report preferring simple parties {{5}} elaborate ones, provided friends are present. Psychologists suggest {{6}} the key ingredient is uninterrupted attention, not expense. Some schools have begun encouraging parents to agree limits — no presents, {{7}} instance, or a fixed guest list. Whether such pacts survive contact {{8}} reality is another matter.
